summary: Platform sidecar ships Go WebRTC remote-control agent; publisher metadata points to 'claude_control' repo under 'ddos' handle
details: sextant-cli-linux-amd64 ships a single 13 MB linux/amd64 Go binary at bin/sxt and no other code. The binary statically links a full WebRTC peer-to-peer stack (pion/webrtc, pion/ice, pion/turn, pion/stun, pion/dtls, pion/sctp, pion/datachannel), the coder/websocket signaling client, and skip2/go-qrcode for out-of-band pairing — the construction of a P2P remote-terminal/remote-control agent, not a local CLI utility. The package.json license field points to https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control, contradicting the neutral 'Sextant CLI' branding on the package and identifying the source repository as 'claude_control' under a user handle prefixed 'ddos'. This sub-package declares no scripts, main, or bin, so `npm install` of it in isolation does not execute anything; the binary is invoked by the parent sextant-cli package that resolves this platform sidecar and runs bin/sxt, at which point a remote peer paired via QR/WebRTC signaling obtains an interactive channel into the host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
